strategy.thesis: Montreal-based specialty pharmaceutical company (TSX: GUD) whose core business is acquiring/in-licensing pharmaceutical products for Canada and select international markets; alongside this it makes strategic limited-partner investments in life-science venture capital funds to gain preferential access to emerging biotech/pharma assets, giving it a direct corporate-strategic-investment nexus to biomedicine.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Invests as an LP in third-party life-science VC funds (e.g. Sectoral Asset Management's New Emerging Medical Opportunities Fund II, Forbion Capital Fund III) rather than running an in-house scientific platform; goal is deal-flow access for its pharmaceutical licensing pipeline.

notable_investments.company: Sectoral New Emerging Medical Opportunities Fund II

summary.en: Montreal-based, TSX-listed specialty pharmaceutical company that, in addition to acquiring and in-licensing drugs for the Canadian and international markets, makes strategic LP investments in life-science venture capital funds (Sectoral's NEMO Fund, Forbion Capital Fund III) to secure preferential access to new pharmaceutical and biotech assets.

name.local: Consortium Québécois sur la Découverte du Médicament

strategy.thesis: Pooled public-private research consortium co-funded by global pharmaceutical companies (Merck, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Amgen, GSK, Roche Canada, Sanofi, Servier, Takeda, Boehringer Ingelheim, Janssen, Lilly, Ono Pharma and others) alongside the Quebec government, sharing project results/costs across members to accelerate drug-discovery technology and de-risk early biopharma R&D in Quebec — a direct pharma-industry strategic co-investment vehicle rather than a single-firm VC.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Funds competitive calls/programs (e.g. SynergiQC, Quantum Leap, Partenar-IA) that support Canadian biotech and academic groups developing enabling drug-discovery technologies, rather than taking direct equity like a classic CVC.

summary.en: Montreal-area, pharma-industry-funded consortium founded in 2008 by Merck, Pfizer and AstraZeneca (now including Amgen, GSK, Roche Canada, Sanofi, Servier, Takeda, Boehringer Ingelheim, Janssen and Lilly) that pools corporate and Quebec-government capital to co-fund early-stage biopharma R&D and drug-discovery technology projects.
summary.local: Consortium québécois cofinancé par de grandes sociétés pharmaceutiques (Merck, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, etc.) et le gouvernement du Québec pour accélérer la découverte de médicaments et l'innovation biopharmaceutique.

verification_notes: CQDM funds R&D projects/technology development rather than taking direct equity in startups in the way a classic CVC does; included here because its capital is directly pooled and governed by operating pharma companies as a strategic collective-investment vehicle for the region, which is the closest fit to this slice's scope. Exact HQ city not confirmed from sources fetched this session (Quebec-based).

strategy.thesis: Not-for-profit drug-development vehicle funded jointly by global pharmaceutical companies (GSK, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson Innovation, Purdue Pharma) and the Quebec government; in-licenses promising academic discoveries from Canadian universities/institutes and funds + develops them (using shared small-molecule and biologics/vaccine R&D facilities) through to human proof-of-concept or partnering — a pharma-consortium-backed company-creation/co-investment model.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Operates two integrated R&D facilities (small-molecule; biologics & vaccines) housed in a former AstraZeneca research site in Montreal, hosting 30+ life-science companies/programs.

summary.en: Montreal not-for-profit founded in 2012 and backed by a consortium of global pharma companies (GSK, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson Innovation, Purdue Pharma) plus the Quebec government; it in-licenses early academic drug-discovery programs from Canadian institutions and funds/develops them toward clinical proof-of-concept, operating shared R&D labs in Montreal.

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture studio of Klick Health — the world's largest independent life-sciences commercialization partner for pharma and biotech brands — providing capital plus in-house commercialization, marketing-advisory and consumer-experience expertise to health/life-science ventures, giving Klick a direct strategic-investment arm anchored in its pharma/biotech client base.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Leverages Klick Health's commercialization, regulatory-marketing and consumer-experience expertise (leadership includes two MDs) rather than an in-house wet-lab platform.

summary.en: Toronto-based venture studio (btwelve, under the Klick Ventures banner) of Klick Health, the world's largest independent life-sciences commercialization partner; provides capital and commercialization expertise to health ventures such as microbiome company Seed Health and healthcare-information platform Ostro.

strategy.thesis: Canadian, TSX/NYSE-listed diversified pharmaceutical and medical-device company (branded/generic pharma, medical devices, OTC); makes selective strategic equity investments in ophthalmology biotech alongside R&D collaborations, e.g. its 2025 investment in Character Biosciences tied to an AMD drug-development partnership.

summary.en: Diversified Canadian pharmaceutical and medical-device company whose eye-health unit Bausch + Lomb makes occasional strategic equity investments in ophthalmology biotechs, including a 2025 investment in Character Biosciences (a $93M Series B round) tied to an AMD therapeutics collaboration.

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture capital arm of MDS Inc. (a Toronto-based Canadian health/life-sciences company spanning clinical diagnostics, MDS Nordion radiopharmaceuticals and MDS Pharma Services CRO); operated as one of the largest North American VC platforms focused exclusively on private healthcare and life-sciences companies across pharma, biotech, medical devices and health IT, at both early and later stages.

summary.en: Historical (1988–mid-2000s) Toronto-based venture capital arm of MDS Inc., a Canadian diagnostics/radiopharmaceuticals/CRO health-sciences company; ran dedicated healthcare/life-science funds (with CPPIB as an LP/co-investor) before its management company, Medical Discovery Management Corporation, was sold to Impax Capital Corp in 2006.
